How to Configure and Install the 4th Axis Module

In this video, we are guided through installing and configuring the 4th axis module on the Carvera Desktop CNC by Makera! The optional 4th axis allows for users to expand what is possible as the Carvera can rotate stock during machining for more complex geometry and production techniques.
How to Configure and Install the 4th Axis Module (Harmonic Drive Version)

In this video, we are guided through installing and configuring the updated 4th axis module with harmonic drive on the Carvera Desktop CNC by Makera! This updated and optional 4th axis allows uses a harmonic drive reducer for increased torque and reduced backlash under maximum load, offering greater performance when machining harder materials like metal.

As shown in this tutorial and supporting guides, users with a Carvera that's serial number starts with C1 will also need to install the wiring adapter in order to use the 4th Axis with Harmonic Drive, as well as update the machines firmware.

How and When to use Air Assist

In this video, we are guided through how and when we should use the air assist module on the Carvera Desktop CNC by Makera! The air assist module allows for users to work with a wide range of materials and methods, like laser engraving or machining metal. Typically we use the air assist module to reduce scorch marks or burns, or to keep our bits cool for chip evacuation.
What is Scan Margin?

In this video, we are introduced to the Scan Margin feature on the Carvera Desktop CNC by Makera! Scan Margin allows for users to have greater success and ease of use when setting up a design to machined. When enabled, Scan Margin will automatically trace the perimeter of our designs using a laser pointer built into the wireless Z probe.

In this video, we are introduced to the Auto Leveling feature on the Carvera Desktop CNC by Makera! Auto Leveling allows for users to automatically calibrate the z height of our stock across multiple points. The Carvera then uses these points to map the changes in thickness and compensate automatically during machining.

What is the PCB Fabrication Pack?
Printed Circuit Boards, or PCBs, are crucial components in nearly very device and appliance we own. The
PCB Fabrication pack
provides all of the materials and tools needed to manufacture complex PCBs using the Carvera.
As shown in the
LED Light example project
, we can make PCBs that are simple or complex by applying a UV solder mask. A solder mask insulates our PCBs which enables us to create more complex and professional quality electronic prototypes.
The Carvera CNC is also compatible with a wide range of

Adding Lubrication to the Carvera
When?
If your machine makes unusual noises during operation, or after frequent use for more than three months, we recommend you check the lubrication condition of the rails and screws on each axis.
If you find that the surfaces of the rails or screws are dry and lack lubricating oil, you need to add lubricant. If they are adequately lubricated, no additional lubricant is required.
1. For safety purposes, replace the cutting tool on the main spindle with a non-cutting tool.
2. Move the machine to the clearance position, unscrew the fixing screws on the rear side of the middle dust cover, and loosen the two screws nearby.
3. Move the machine to anchor1, unscrew the fixing screws on the front side of the middle dust cover, and loosen the two screws nearby.
4. Pull out the middle dust cover forward.

5. After cleaning the lower part of the machine from dust, use a syringe to lubricate the cylindrical slider, lead screw nut, and the lead screw with lubricating oil. Please use guide rail oil or low viscosity lubricating grease. Insert the syringe needle into the dust seal of the cylindrical slider and inject lubricating oil until a small amount of lubricating oil overflows. Then, insert the syringe needle into the dust seal of the lead screw nut, inject lubricating oil, and apply a small amount of lubricating oil on the lead screw.
6. Move the machine to the clearance position, and use the same method to lubricate the rear part of the Y-axis.
7. Repeat the process of moving the machine to the clearance position and anchor1, two to three times.
8. Reinstall the middle dust cover on the machine. Be sure to place the dust cloth underneath both sides of the dust cover during installation.
9. Move the machine to anchor1, remove the dust cloth pressing plate on the right side of the X-axis.

10. Unscrew the lubrication hole screws on the linear slide block, use a syringe to inject lubricating oil into the linear slide block, and tighten the screws. Then, use the same method as the X-axis to lubricate the lead screw nut and lead screw.
11. Reinstall the dust cloth pressing plate on the right side of the X-axis.
12. Move the machine to the clearance position, and use the same method to operate the left side of the X-axis.
13. Repeat the process of moving the machine to the clearance position and anchor1, two to three times.
14. Move the machine to anchor2,and lower the Z-axis to the lowest possible position.
15. Remove the upper dust cloth of the Z-axis and lubricate the upper part of the Z-axis, following the same method as the X-axis.

16. Move the machine to anchor2, remove the lower dust cloth of the Z-axis, and lubricate the lower part of the Z-axis. Please note that the lower part of the Z-axis operation may be a bit challenging, so proceed slowly.
17. After lubrication, install the lower dust cloth of the Z-axis and move the Z-axis up and down two to three times.
A clean machine is a happy machine.
Use a vacuum or compressed air to clean the machine's surfaces to remove dust, debris, and any accumulated material.
Move the X and Y-axis to clean areas under the bed and carriage.
Make sure you use a clean cloth when wiping the acrylic cover, Small particles could cause scratches.
Pay special attention to the ATC area, any debris might interfere with the ATC process.
Clean under the machine, some debris does make its way to the bottom of the machine.
Empty the dust bin regularly, and vacuum or use compressed air to clean and unblock the filter mesh.

Converting from Reverse-Jaw Chuck to Forward-Jaw Chuck:

1. Loosen the chuck by rotating it until the jaws can be taken out. Please be cautious, as the rear nut will become very tight just before the jaws are almost completely loosened. You'll need to manually pry the jaws outward.
2. After removing all the jaws, observe the numbering on each jaw. The correct order for the forward-jaw chuck is No.1 - No.2 - No.3 - No.4.
3. When installing the forward-jaw chuck, rotate the rear nut of the chuck and align the notch on the nut with any of the slots. Then, insert No.1 jaw and rotate the rear nut.
4. Rotate the rear nut 90° and insert No.2 jaw into the next slot.

5. Please note that at this point, the jaws have limited contact with the slots, resulting in weaker sliding ability. Gently shake the jaws manually to align them inward before turning the rear nut again.
